newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Model child made 1990s Vietnam hero.
newsitem.headline: Model child made 1990s Vietnam hero.

text.p: Vietnam sought to rekindle patriotic and revolutionary fervour on Friday by announcing that a model child who gave his life to defeat foreign aggressors was a national hero.
Kim Dong (Bronze Metal), born Nong Van Den, was shot dead in 1943 while trying to warn a gathering of Viet Minh guerrillas in the northern province of Cao Bang, about the approach of French troops.
The Hanoi Moi newspaper said he was now being formally recognised for the act, more than 50 years later, following a petition from members of the Communist Youth Pioneers movement.
"This important event proves that the Party, the State, always evaluates correctly the contribution of young martyrs," the paper quoted a Communist Youth league official as saying.

Vietnam's history has been one of domination by and uprising against foreign powers. City streets throughout the country are named after key figures in the process, most of whom helped fend off Chinese aggressors.
